title: Security review — Encryption, KMS/BYOK/HSM (Astral Bank)
summary: High-level security review focused on encryption at rest and in transit, options for KMS integrations and BYOK/HSM, audit logging, and data residency. Customer wants clear path for hardware-backed keys (HSM) and proof points for key separation and zeroization. Agreed next steps: share KMS/BYOK architecture doc, SOC 2 report, schedule HSM integration demo/POC, and provide a short checklist for legal procurement.
topics: Audit logs and key access auditing
Data residency and private deployment options

transcript:
Date: 2026-08-14 UTC 16:00
Duration: ~50 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE); Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE); Dmitri Volkov (Redwood SE - observing); Priya Kapoor (Astral Bank Head of Security); Samir Patel (Platform); Jocelyn Park (Compliance); Ethan Wu (SRE)

Summary (auto): security review focused on encryption, KMS, BYOK, HSM. Customer questions about key separation, rotation, auditability, and private deployment.

00:00 Lena: ok hey everyone thanks for joining, uh this is Lena from Redwood. this is Marco, our se, and Dmitri's joining too, we'll go through high level and then deep dive on KMS/HSM.
00:18 Priya: thanks Lena, quick context — Astral Bank is evaluating inference infra for customer-facing fraud models. main constraints: keys must be customer-managed, FIPS-backed HSM highly preferred, and full audit trail for any key usage. we have strict data residency, cannot move certain pii across eu-west-1.
00:37 Lena: makes sense. quick question on deployment mode — are you leaning hosted api, dedicated, or private?
00:42 Samir: For pilot we'd like dedicated but we need the option to go private (VPC or on-prem) for production if we cannot prove key separation with hosted.
00:51 Marco: got it. i'll sketch how our options map to KMS. hosted api — we offer tenant isolation and we can integrate with customer-managed KMS via BYOK on supported clouds; Dedicated gives reserved capacity with network controls; Private (VPC/on-prem) lets you hold keys entirely in your environment and we integrate via HSM connectors.
01:24 Priya: can you clarify "integrate with customer-managed KMS" — does Redwood hold any plaintext keys or key material in hosted mode?
01:34 Lena: no, Redwood never holds customer key material when BYOK/HSM is configured. we store encrypted data blobs that are encrypted with a data encryption key which is wrapped by your KMS key. The wrap/unwrap calls happen against your KMS — in hosted we call your KMS over TLS and only the wrapped dek is stored.
01:56 Jocelyn: what about key rotation and revocation — if we rotate keys do you support immediate rewrap? what happens to old ciphertext?
02:06 Marco: good Q. We support key rotation flows: we can re-encrypt stored prefixes/objects asynchronously; existing wrapped data remains decryptable as long as KMS can unwrap old key versions. we also support a rewrap job during migration. immediate revocation will prevent future unwraps; you can set a grace window.
02:38 Ethan: and HSM specifics — we require HSM-backed keys (PCI/FIPS). do you have certifications or can you integrate with our on-prem HSM?
02:47 Lena: yes we support HSM-backed keys via standard KMIP/CloudHSM connectors and cloud KMS providers (AWS KMS w/ CloudHSM, Azure Key Vault Managed HSM, GCP HSM). For private deployment we can run a connector in your VPC that talks to your HSM over secure channel so keys never leave your boundary.
03:12 Priya: can you describe the actual call flow in hosted with BYOK? i want to understand where the plaintext DEK exists and who ever sees it.
03:23 Marco: sure. flows: 1) Redwood generates a data encryption key (DEK) locally in the runtime pod memory, encrypts the payload, then calls customer KMS to wrap the DEK — the wrapped DEK is stored. The plaintext DEK exists transiently in memory only and is zeroized after use. We have KMS access logs for wrap/unwrap events; all network traffic is TLS 1.2/1.3.
03:57 Priya: zeroization — can you prove DEK zeroization? is it OS-level secure erase or memory overwrite?
04:06 Marco: it's an application memory overwrite pattern followed by freeing the buffer. on dedicated/private we can use kernel features and mlock to avoid swapping. for higher assurance we support hardware-backed enclave options in private deployments (discussion and POC needed).
04:33 Jocelyn: audit logs — we need immutable audit logs of key usage and an API we can ingest to our SIEM.
04:40 Lena: we surface audit logs for KMS operations and provide a push or s3 export; logs include wrap/unwrap timestamps, principal, and pod id. we also have platform audit logs for control plane actions. they can be routed to your log account or exported to your s3 with retention options.
05:04 Priya: are those logs tamper-evident?
05:09 Marco: we support signed/immutable log delivery (append-only) and integration with your log ingestion for long-term retention. we can also provide raw events for your SIEM.
05:28 Samir: about network — in hosted mode, how do you secure calls to our KMS? do you require a peered VPC or public endpoint?
05:36 Lena: we support both. for highest security we recommend private endpoints/peering (PrivateLink for AWS) so KMS traffic never traverses public internet. TLS mutual auth is optional and recommended for dedicated/private links.
05:57 Priya: what about compliance — SOC2/ISO attestation?
06:03 Lena: Redwood has SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001; we'll share the latest report. our SOC 2 covers key management controls as part of encryption and access controls but we can highlight the sections most relevant to BYOK/HSM.
06:21 Jocelyn: please send the scoping doc. also any pen test reports?
06:26 Lena: yes we'll include the pen test executive summary.
06:31 Dmitri: quick note on FIPS — our HSM integrations can use FIPS-validated modules; for cloud KMS there are FIPS endpoints and managed HSM options.
06:45 Ethan: latency question — wrapping/unwrapping on every request will add overhead. how do you minimize per-token cost/latency?
06:54 Marco: we never call KMS per token. we keep a DEK in memory and reuse it for a short TTL with encryption context; we use KV cache and continuous batching to keep throughput. unwraps happen on key rotation or cold starts. so the KMS QPS is low.
07:20 Priya: what's the rotation cadence you recommend?
07:24 Marco: typical is 30–90 days for DEK rotation, CMK rotation per policy; we support automated rotation workflows with your KMS and can trigger rewrap jobs.
07:36 Samir: do you support customer-provided root key material (BYOK upload) for cloud KMS import or do you require external HSM?
07:45 Lena: depends on provider. AWS KMS supports importing key material for certain types; many customers prefer CloudHSM-backed keys. for highest assurance we recommend a hardware-backed key that never leaves your HSM (no import). we support both patterns.
08:03 Jocelyn: legal care — we need contract language for key custody and indemnity around key compromise. who in Redwood handles that?
08:11 Lena: our legal and security team will provide suggested SLO/clauses — i'll introduce you to our security/contact legal during next week.
08:20 Priya: can you run through a short threat model — if someone at Redwood is compromised, can they ever decrypt our customer data?
08:28 Marco: short answer: not with BYOK/HSM. If keys are customer-managed and never exported, Redwood cannot unwrap DEKs without access to your KMS/HSM. for hosted mode if you provide credentials or grant access via a service account we only have the ability you grant; we recommend least-privilege IAM roles and restricted service principals.
08:57 Priya: is there support for key attestation or hardware attestation?
09:02 Dmitri: yes for private deployments we can attest via HSM certificates and TPM attestation flows; we can provide measurement quotes and POC for attestation.
09:24 Samir: do you keep any plaintext logs or diagnostic dumps that might contain data?
09:31 Marco: no plaintext logs for user payload; logs are redacted and we provide a diagnostic mode that scrubs sensitive fields. we can also run diagnostics in your environment to avoid data leaving your boundary.
09:50 Jocelyn: regulatory — for EU user data we need data at rest in eu-west-1 only. can you pin nodes/hosts to a region?
09:58 Lena: yes we support regional pinning and can ensure model serving and storage stay in your chosen region. for private deployments you control region entirely.
10:12 Priya: about HSM key lifecycle — what about zeroization if we decommission?
10:17 Marco: keys in an HSM can be zeroized per vendor procedures; we support key destruction workflows and can provide cert of destruction from the HSM vendor where possible.
10:30 Ethan: how about backups of wrapped keys — if you store wrapped DEKs, are those included in backups and do you replicate them cross-region?
10:38 Marco: wrapped DEKs are part of encrypted objects and we replicate according to region policy; we can disable cross-region replication for certain data classes. backups are encrypted and we can restrict replication based on tags.
10:55 Priya: do you have references or customers in financial services using BYOK/HSM?
11:02 Lena: yes we have multiple banks — we'll share redacted architecture references and a short case study.
11:10 Jocelyn: on SOC2 — which trust principles cover key management?
11:15 Lena: primarily security and availability; we'll point to the control IDs in the report.
11:23 Priya: any penalties if keys are compromised due to Redwood misconfig?
11:27 Lena: that goes into contract; we'll have legal provide standard indemnity language and we can negotiate enterprise terms.
11:35 Dmitri: quick note on performance — for high-throughput inference we rely on continuous batching and pinned DEKs in memory to keep TLS/KMS calls minimal.
11:44 Samir: will you support a dedicated path where KMS calls go over an internal private link? we want to avoid public endpoints entirely.
11:52 Marco: yes PrivateLink/Private Endpoint fully supported; for on-prem we can do direct peering or a connector appliance.
12:05 Priya: what about key access policies — can we limit which Redwood services/pods can call unwrap?
12:12 Marco: yes we surface a per-route principal identity and RBAC mapping — you can scope keys to service principals. we also provide mTLS and IAM policies on the connector.
12:32 Jocelyn: for compliance we need proof of separation of duties — can you show role mappings and admin access logs?
12:39 Lena: yes we provide admin audit logs, role definition export and we can map to your LDAP/SAML for SSO.
12:50 Priya: SSO — does Redwood support SAML and SCIM provisioning?
12:55 Lena: yes both SAML 2.0 for SSO and SCIM for user provisioning + fine grained RBAC.
13:10 Ethan: question on encryption in transit — TLS versions and cipher suites?
13:14 Marco: we support TLS 1.2+ and 1.3, modern ciphers. we can disable old ciphers per enterprise config.
13:28 Priya: any plan for hardware attestation logs or signed audit records?
13:33 Dmitri: yes we can produce signed event logs and hardware attestation reports for private or dedicated setups.
13:44 Samir: procurement — we'll need a checklist of replacements and legal artifacts to start.
13:50 Jocelyn: yes please include SOC2, pen test, data flow diagrams, encryption architecture, KMS/HSM integration notes and contract clauses.
13:59 Lena: will do. i'll follow up with the doc package and the SOC2 + pen test.
14:06 Priya: one last tech — if we revoke a key, can you guarantee we can shred all cached DEKs fast?
14:12 Marco: we have a kill-switch pattern where we can invalidate cached DEKs and force cold start rewrap; in private setups we can zeroize memory and restart pods. we document procedures.
14:32 Lena: ok wrapping up — agreed actions: we'll send docs, schedule HSM demo, and share references. any final questions?
14:40 Priya: no that's good, thanks.
14:44 Lena: thanks everyone. end.
